To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the set of clusterings of a graph can be characterized as the set of all lifted multicuts and that this leads to a practically relevant insight into the definition of classes by must-join constraints and to a practically relevant metric for comparison.
the set of clusterings of a graph can be characterized as the set of lifted multicutoffs, and that lifted multicuts are a powerful tool to find optimal decompositions.

the lifted multicut formulation of the graph decomposition problem allows for a characterization of the set of all clusterings, for the definition of a metric for comparing clusterings, and for an exact optimization algorithm for the minimum cost clustering problem.
In summary, our research is concerned with

(i) the characterization of decompositions as lifted multicuts, (ii) their comparison by metrics, (iii) the optimization of decompositions defined by must-join constraints and must-cut constraints, (iv) the characterization of some facets of the corresponding lifted multicut polytope, (v) the development of separation procedures, and (vi) the design and implementation of a branch-and-cut algorithm.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we can solve the problem to optimality for small graphs, but for large graphs the problem becomes intractable.
we have established an important link between graph clustering and the theory of multicut polytops.

the lifted multicut formulation is a very powerful and flexible framework for analyzing and finding decompositions of graphs and that the presented algorithms are very efficient for finding optimal decompositions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have established the foundations for a new approach to the analysis and optimization of decompositions.
lifted multicut polyhedra can be solved efficiently and that the set of all clusterings can be characterized and compared by a few must-join and/or must-cut constraints.
we have established a new and useful way of analyzing and optimizing decompositions of graphs, which is based on lifted multicuts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the set of all graph decompositions is a convex polyhedron, and that this polyhedron can be described by a small number of inequalities.
lifted multicuts are an effective tool to study the space of all decompositions and to compute optimal decompositions.
the optimization of lifted multicuts provides a powerful tool to analyze and compute decompositions of graphs.
